title: Reading Drill — Comparing cameras at a nature hide — Building a comparison
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Comparing cameras at a nature hide — Building a comparison
passages.body:
**A** The volunteer observer had been asked to investigate moving birds being missed at the edge of the image in Cairnford. Its first task was to decide which signs of improvement could be compared between sites. It settled on the number of usable clips, because the same measure could be applied in the original setting and at a second location.

**B** During a ten-week comparison, the team used recording samples at both places. It recorded outcomes separately for each site. Because activity at different tides might influence the figures, the team used a column in the record to show when that condition was present. The surveys included quiet periods as well as busy ones.

**C** The team then put forward a wider field of view. Its report asked for another comparison after the change had been tried. This would distinguish a genuine effect from an improvement that could have occurred anyway. The report did not assume that the more successful site before the change would be the better site afterwards.
